_comment: Covered calls' browser tools. AutolaunchWeb.ToolManifest adds them to tool_manifest.json only while the site offers covered calls (AUTOLAUNCH_COVERED_CALLS=true). A public tool's `request` is the HTTP request it makes: `path` with each {field} filled from its input, and `body` the input fields it posts.

tools.name: autolaunch_covered_call_listings
tools.title: List covered calls on a stock
tools.description: List the covered calls on one Base stock token, as its contract holds them at the latest block: every listing with its seller, strike_per_token and premium_per_token (micro-USDC per whole token), expiry (a Friday at 21:00 UTC, Unix seconds), amount, filled and available (raw token units, unit per whole token) and stage (open, sold, exercise or closed), the stock's multiplier and its reference price. Reads only; needs no sign-in. The reading is shared and may be up to five minutes old; read_at says when it was taken.

symbol.description: The stock token's symbol exactly as the site lists it, such as AMZNc.

tools.name: autolaunch_covered_call_quote
tools.title: Suggest a covered-call premium
tools.description: Quote a covered call on one Base stock token before listing it, for a weekly expiry: the stock's reference price (spot_per_token, micro-USDC per whole token) and when its feed last updated it; the next four weekly expiries, each with its exercise window (Unix seconds), and the chosen one's term in whole days (term_days); three suggested strikes above the reference price (presets), each with how far above it is as a fraction and a suggested premium per whole token; and, for the chosen strike (the middle suggestion when none is given) and premium (the suggestion when none is given), what a listing of amount raw token units pays if all of it is bought at once and all of it exercised (receipt): the premium, the 1% fee, what the seller keeps, the strike, the stock's worth at the reference price, and the premium kept as a fraction of that worth for the term (net_premium_yield, not a yearly rate). Without an amount the per-token figures still come back and the totals are null. Every USDC figure is what the contract counts, rounded up. A guide for a seller only: the contract enforces no suggestion, and the quote is refused while the reference price is more than four days old. Reads only; needs no sign-in.

symbol.description: The stock token's symbol exactly as the site lists it, such as AMZNc.

expiry.description: A Friday at 21:00 UTC, as Unix seconds; listings take no other expiry.

amount.description: Raw stock units to list; unit raw units make one whole token. Leave it out for the per-token figures only.

strike_per_token.description: The strike in micro-USDC (6 decimals) per whole token. Leave it out for the middle suggested strike.

premium_per_token.description: The premium the listing asks, in micro-USDC per whole token. Leave it out for the suggested premium.

tools.name: autolaunch_my_covered_calls
tools.title: Read my covered calls on a stock
tools.description: Read my person's covered calls on one Base stock token, for their signed-in wallet, at the latest block: the listings it sold, on every listing the calls it may exercise (held) and the stock it may claim (claimable), and the stock in the wallet itself (balance), the most it can list now, in raw token units. Changes nothing. Prepare the exact request, sign it with your existing SIWA signer, then provide input, request and proof. Browser sign-in is not agent authority.

symbol.description: The stock token's symbol exactly as the site lists it, such as AMZNc.

tools.name: autolaunch_covered_call_prepare
tools.title: Prepare a covered-call step
tools.description: Prepare the wallet steps for one covered-call action on a Base stock token: list (amount, strike_per_token, premium_per_token, expiry), fill (listing_id, amount), exercise (listing_id, amount), cancel, claim or collect_strike (listing_id). The steps are for one of my person's own wallets: signer when given, otherwise the wallet they signed in with; any other wallet is refused. The site only prepares: the wallet's own key signs and sends each step in turn (to, data, value on chain), and money moves only then. approved says whether the allowance already covers the action; blocked names, in code and words, a reason the chain's current state makes the action certain to fail, and the steps are still returned. Changes nothing. Prepare the exact request, sign it with your existing SIWA signer, then provide input, request and proof. Browser sign-in is not agent authority.

symbol.description: The stock token's symbol exactly as the site lists it, such as AMZNc.

listing_id.description: The listing's number on this market, for every kind but list.

amount.description: Raw stock token units: to list, to buy (fill) or to exercise.

strike_per_token.description: For list: the strike in micro-USDC per whole token.

premium_per_token.description: For list: the minimum premium in micro-USDC per whole token.

expiry.description: For list: a Friday at 21:00 UTC, as Unix seconds.

signer.description: One of my person's own wallet addresses, 0x and 40 hex digits. Omit it to use the wallet they signed in with.
